summary.headline: Monte Carlo Q4 FY26 revenue rose 36% to about INR280 crores and EBITDA margin hit 9.2%; FY26 revenue up 16% to INR1,276 crores, with FY27 guidance deferred to Q2.
summary.overview: Management reported Q4 FY26 revenue of about INR280 crores (up 36% YoY), EBITDA of INR26 crores (9.2% margin) and PAT of INR5 crores versus a loss of INR10 crores a year earlier. For FY26, revenue rose 16% to INR1,276 crores, EBITDA was about INR227 crores (17.81% margin ex other income) and PAT was INR112 crores (up 38%, 8.79% margin). Management said FY26 hit its guidance of 16% revenue growth, and attributed the Q4 turnaround to lower discounts, summer-season sales and provisioning taken in Q3. Management declined to give FY27 numeric guidance until the Q2 call, but reiterated that double-digit growth is on the cards.

segments.name: Rock.it brand
segments.commentary: Gross sales grew 86% in FY26, per management, which described it as consistent through the year.

segments.name: Footwear
segments.commentary: Gross sales rose 149% versus FY25; management targets doubling footwear turnover, mainly online, plus about 15 Reliance large-format stores and 30-35 larger EBOs being retrofitted.

segments.name: Home Textile
segments.commentary: Maintained robust growth; about 12% of FY26 revenue, with management guiding to 13-14% of revenue in FY27.

segments.name: Online
segments.commentary: Net sales grew 38% versus FY25 across own website and external portals; quick commerce tie-ups with Blinkit, Swiggy and Zepto, with BigBasket in final talks.

segments.name: Kids
segments.commentary: Annual revenue run-rate of about INR110 crores, up from about INR100 crores.

segments.name: Product mix
segments.commentary: FY26 mix: winter wear 45%, non-winter/summer 42%, textiles about 10.2%, accessories and footwear 2%.

segments.name: Renewable energy (IPP)
segments.commentary: PPA of about 40 MW signed with Madhya Pradesh government; capex INR130-140 crores; expected revenue INR115-160 crores per year; billing to start in FY27 (within about 12 months). Management said IRR is above 15%.

guidance_outlook: FY27 numeric revenue and profit guidance deferred to the Q2 FY27 call; management reiterated double-digit revenue growth for FY27.
Store expansion: 40-45 gross EBO openings in FY27, possibly up to 50; no store closures planned, so gross and net additions should be close.
Management declined to guide Q1 FY27 profitability or quarterly revenue; said Q1 typically carries about 12-13% of annual revenue due to winter returns.
EBITDA margin expected to remain around 20% including other income, per management.
Renewable (IPP/BESS) projects will be pursued only where IRR is at least 15-17%; capex in manufacturing expected at INR10-15 crores a year.
capex_capacity: Solar IPP: 35 MW AC (about 43-45 MW with 30% overloading, feasibility pending), PPA at INR2.79 per unit, non-DCR modules; capex about INR130-140 crores, funded 75% debt and 25% equity; financial closure expected in 7-10 days; commissioning within about 12 months.

Store network: 497 EBOs at year end; 2 new Cloak & Decker EBOs added in Q4 (24 Cloak & Decker stores total); 14-15 loss-making stores closed in FY25; average store size 1,000-1,500 sq ft; about 50 stores above 2,000 sq ft.
Manufacturing: about 85% of production outsourced to vendors across India; in-house capex of INR10-15 crores a year.
Inventory of about INR570 crores, with management saying inventory levels will stay high given the shift to SIS, large-format and online sales.
demand_pricing: Summer categories are growing faster than winter; management cited wider penetration across regions and loyalty customers from winter range buying summer products.
Raw material (cotton, wool) costs rose; management said it covered inputs before the trade show and took a 6-8% price hike, so margins should not be affected.
Management reported no significant consumer spending cut so far, but flagged fuel price hikes and inflation as risks.
Returns were about 17% of gross sales in FY26, above the earlier expected lower level; management said returns are market-driven.
Middle East export trial was 2,500-3,000 pieces, 70% sold in the secondary market; repeat orders delayed 2-3 months due to regional uncertainty.
Channel inventory described as comfortable at the company, store and channel partner levels; pre-winter and winter bookings were continuing with no booking growth figure disclosed.
Management dismissed fast-fashion competition (Zara, Shein), citing 10+ years of presence in India.

qa_highlights.question: How much of Q4 revenue growth came from volume, and what drove it?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said volume grew 12% on an annual basis; growth was driven by summer categories, and FY26 revenue rose 16% against guidance of 15%.

qa_highlights.question: Did the company see any consumer spending slowdown from inflation?
qa_highlights.answer: No major spending cut so far; management flagged that further fuel price increases could hit consumer spending.

qa_highlights.question: What are the details of the renewable energy project?
qa_highlights.answer: About 40 MW PPA with Madhya Pradesh; capex INR130-140 crores, 75% debt; expected revenue INR115-160 crores a year; management cited IRR of 15-16% over 25 years.

qa_highlights.question: Is the KUSUM subsidy available and included in IRR?
qa_highlights.answer: No; the project uses non-DCR modules, which are about 30% cheaper, and so it does not qualify for the INR1.05 crore per MW CFA subsidy available to DCR modules.

qa_highlights.question: Why did EBO count rise only 26 net in the last 10 years, and is the 40-45 store target gross or net?
qa_highlights.answer: The 40-45 target is gross; FY25 included a one-off closure of 14-15 unprofitable stores, and management expects gross and net to be close in FY27.

qa_highlights.question: Why is inventory still high at about INR570 crores?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory days fell to 144 from 169, but management said levels will stay high as sales shift to SIS, large-format and online channels, where inventory sits with partners until sold.

qa_highlights.question: Is raw material inflation passed through to customers?
qa_highlights.answer: Yes, immediately; the company covers raw materials before trade shows and took a 6-8% price hike on uncovered items, so management expects no margin impact.

qa_highlights.question: What is the Q1 seasonality and returns pattern?
qa_highlights.answer: Q1 carries about 12-13% of annual revenue because winter returns come in April-May; management would not give quarterly revenue guidance.

risks_watch: Fuel price hikes and inflation could cut consumer spending; management said geopolitical tensions are the main headwind.
Returns rose to 17% of gross sales in FY26 from 15%, and management expects heavy returns in Q1; this could weigh on Q1 FY27 revenue and profitability.
Solar IPP financial closure (7-10 days) and commissioning (about 12 months); final capex, overloading and IRR are still unconfirmed.
Inventory at 144 days remains high; management expects it to stay elevated as the channel mix shifts.
Middle East export repeat orders delayed 2-3 months.
The Q2 FY27 call is the next formal guidance point for numeric targets.
summary.management_tone: Confident on FY26 delivery and the Q4 turnaround, but evasive on FY27 numbers, repeatedly deferring specific revenue and profit guidance to the Q2 call citing geopolitical and inflation uncertainty.
